headline: Risks of Unlicensed Work and Consumer Protection Guidance
articleBody: Unlicensed or improperly supervised bathroom renovation work can expose Los Angeles County homeowners to financial, safety, and legal risks. The California Contractors State License Board (CSLB) warns that unlicensed individuals may lack required knowledge of building codes, permitting, and safety practices, increasing the likelihood of substandard work. Bathrooms involve plumbing, electrical, and waterproofing systems, so errors can lead to leaks, mold, electrical hazards, or structural damage that may not be immediately apparent. From a financial standpoint, consumer protection agencies and insurance industry guidance note that homeowners may have limited recourse if an unlicensed contractor performs defective work or abandons a project. Licensed contractors in California must carry a contractor’s bond, and consumers may have access to administrative complaint processes through CSLB; these mechanisms generally do not apply to unlicensed operators. Some homeowners’ insurance policies may also exclude coverage for damages arising from unpermitted or non‑code‑compliant work. Liability for worker injuries is another concern. If a worker is injured on site and the contractor does not have workers’ compensation insurance, legal and insurance commentary explains that the homeowner may be treated as the employer and could face claims for medical costs and lost wages. This risk is one reason CSLB emphasizes verifying workers’ compensation coverage for any contractor with employees. To mitigate these risks, agencies like CSLB and the Federal Trade Commission advise consumers to hire properly licensed contractors, verify license status and insurance, insist on pulling appropriate permits, and avoid large cash payments. They recommend documenting the project via written contracts, change orders, and inspection approvals and caution against splitting a job into smaller contracts to stay under licensing thresholds—all practices sometimes used by unlicensed operators to evade regulation.
